solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Merry and encouraging, not revolting

indicators.note: 'not revolting' asks for the word that means rising in revolt to be taken away

parts.note: encouraging and helpful
a population that is up is in revolt, as in 'up in arms'

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful and supportive who has no wish to rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Take UP out of SUPPORTIVE to leave SPORTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means playful or frolicsome, a close synonym of merry.

clue.text: Bird has turned up to grab catch, taking more risks

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it, so the reversed word wraps around the next piece
in a down entry, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to get is to catch, as with a ball or a bus
more rash, more reckless

explanation.surface: A bird appears, ready to grab its prey, behaving ever more daringly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' sounds like the bird's prey, but it is just a verb for obtaining. The reversed word wraps around it before the comparative adjective is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The sage thrasher is a small grey-brown songbird of the western American sagebrush country.

clue.text: Tree map involving appropriate technology

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it inside, so one word encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
AT is the standard abbreviation for appropriate technology

explanation.surface: A chart showing trees, plotted with suitably modest technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree map' reads as one phrase, but the break comes after 'Tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Platan is an old name for the plane tree, from the Latin platanus.

clue.text: Striker in school for swats wanting head dismissed

indicators.note: having the head sent away means the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a crammer is a school that drills students intensively for exams; a swot (here spelt swat) is someone who studies hard

explanation.surface: A footballer at a hothouse school, unhappy that the headteacher was sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: CRAMMER loses its C. 'Striker' looks like a footballer but means something that strikes or rams.
explanation.definitionFit: A rammer is a tool for ramming or driving things home, so it strikes as it works.

clue.text: Horrible rodent has bitten Henry in the seat

indicators.note: a mouth that has bitten something holds it inside, so the rearranged letters close around the next piece
something horrible is badly made, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A nasty rat has bitten Henry on his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the seat' suggests a bitten bottom, but it means enthroned; it is an adjective phrase, matching throned.
explanation.definitionFit: Throned means seated on a throne, holding power, which is what being in the seat of authority describes.

clue.text: Perform in vessel in underground water

definitions.note: adjective: describes water held in the ground above the water table

indicators.note: the first in places one word inside the container word that follows

parts.note: a vase is a vessel
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Putting on a performance in a boat floating on a buried lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' puts one word inside the other; the second only joins the wordplay to the definition, which is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Vadose is the geologists' term for water in the zone between the surface and the water table.

clue.text: Wife and husband almost glow at what location in Scotland?

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
H is the abbreviation for husband
an aura is a glow surrounding something

explanation.surface: A married couple, nearly radiant, asking where they are in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Whaur is the Scots spelling and pronunciation of where, meaning at what place.

clue.text: African money invested in serious entertainment

indicators.note: money invested in something is placed inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Putting cash from Africa into a highbrow show.
explanation.definitionFit: The sente is a small coin of Lesotho, one hundredth of a loti.

clue.text: Papal licence, one not dated, with bits of unusual Latin terminology

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
n.d. means no date, used in bibliographies for an undated item

indicators.note: bits of the following words are small pieces of them, here their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A Vatican permission, undated, written in odd ecclesiastical Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: An indult is a licence granted by the Pope permitting something the general church law does not allow.

clue.text: New marking fools on square may get in army unit, US soldier excepted

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the pieces go inside the unit
something excepted is left out, so the soldier is removed from the unit

parts.note: a regiment is an army unit
a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece being on another means it sits right after it

parts.note: asses are fools
S is an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Idiots on a parade ground join a regiment with no Americans in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier is taken out of the unit first, then the fools with their square go into the gap that is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A reassessment is a fresh evaluation, as when an exam script is graded a second time.

clue.text: Dancers getting relief, stifling expression of joy?

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, holding something closed inside

parts.note: alms are charitable relief for the poor
ah is a cry of pleasure; the question mark admits it can mean other things

explanation.surface: Performers being given charity while suppressing their delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relief' suggests comfort, but here it means charitable giving to the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Almahs (or almehs) are Egyptian professional dancing girls.

clue.text: Around edge of country spots old hybrid animals

indicators.note: one word goes around the selected letter, enclosing it

parts.note: moles are spots on the skin

indicators.note: an edge is an extremity, here the last letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter of country

explanation.surface: Pockmarked creatures of mixed breed found at the edge of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLES wraps round Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Moyle is an obsolete word for a mule, the cross between a donkey and a horse.

clue.text: One of the Scots embracing the goddess

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, holding something within one's arms

parts.note: ane is Scots for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman hugging a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the Scots' marks a Scots word, and the word 'the' straight after it is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Animal in hollow place nipped by nasty adder

indicators.note: being nipped means being bitten, held between the jaws
something nasty is twisted out of shape, so the snake's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a pan is a natural hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A creature in a burrow is bitten by a vicious snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda is a small reddish mammal of the Himalayas, distinct from the giant panda.

clue.text: My note about true origin of word

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's memo about where a word really comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: An etymon is the original root form from which a later word derives; the Greek etymon means the true sense.

clue.text: African shelter by university

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A hut in Africa standing next to a university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a Hutu is an African.

clue.text: Faculty making some money once

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a natural gift or ability
second meaning: an ancient weight and unit of currency

explanation.surface: A university department that used to earn a sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department, but here it means an aptitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is a talent; in ancient Greece and the Bible a talent was also a large sum of silver.

clue.text: Afflictions when banking pounds or bucks

indicators.note: banking money means holding it, so one word keeps the other inside

parts.note: sores are painful afflictions of the skin
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Troubles when depositing sterling or dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' and 'bucks' both look like money; bucks are male deer here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorel is a buck, a male fallow deer, in its third year.

clue.text: Volcanic material destroying reptile

indicators.note: destroying the creature breaks it apart, letting its letters be reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lava pouring out and killing a lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Perlite is a glassy volcanic rock, often expanded for use in horticulture and insulation.

clue.text: Herbs and grass, mostly in America

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: rice is a cereal grass
taken as written
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: Plants and turf grown mainly across the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' looks like the location, but both words supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricinus is the plant genus containing the castor-oil plant, so it names a group of herbs.

clue.text: Private home with hospital facility

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a ward is a room for patients in a hospital

explanation.surface: A private house fitted with its own hospital wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inward can mean internal or intimate, so inward thoughts are private ones.

clue.text: Time off — trade's abandoned with family finally seen?

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the selected letter is added on at the end
something abandoned has run wild, freed from its usual order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: what is finally seen of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of family

explanation.surface: A holiday when work is dropped and the family finally gets a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest day is a day free from work or competition, which is a break from duty.

clue.text: Fantastic eleven getting carried away?

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, imaginatively reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant football team swept up in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'carried away' means abducted, not overexcited.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlevé is French for abducted or kidnapped, literally removed by force.

clue.text: Debater stirring our rage, nothing less

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged
less means without, so the round letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A disputant inflaming people's anger without any restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from OURRAGE, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An arguer is a person who argues a case, which is what a debater does.

clue.text: Girl lacking energy in improvised singing

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Georgia is a girl's name
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A girl without much energy for impromptu singing.
explanation.walkthrough: GEORGIA without its E leaves GORGIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgia is the 16th and 17th century term for rapid improvised vocal ornamentation.

clue.text: Fish — a shiny group brought aboard ship

indicators.note: something brought aboard goes inside the vessel

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
Argo was a large constellation, a group of shining stars, now split into smaller ones

explanation.surface: A shoal of glittering fish hauled onto a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A shiny group' reads like a shoal but is a constellation; the ship Argo also gives the constellation its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargos are sea breams of the genus Diplodus, so they are fish.

clue.text: Tree worker, one by a river?

parts.note: a worker ant, the commonest crossword worker
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A forester standing beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The antiar is the upas tree of Java, whose sap was used as an arrow poison.

clue.text: Top-notch fabric used up to make ribbon

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as the letter I
net is an open-mesh fabric

explanation.surface: The finest cloth worn out to make a ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: AINET written upwards gives TENIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenia (taenia) is a headband or ribbon in classical dress, and also a tapeworm, from its ribbon shape.

clue.text: Tribe shows formality leading province

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, stiff formality
Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A tribe shows ceremony while in charge of a region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were the ancient British tribe of East Anglia led by Boudicca.

clue.text: African community was backing chamber orchestra

indicators.note: backing something means coming behind it, so this word follows the next piece

parts.note: ECO is the English Chamber Orchestra
taken as written

explanation.surface: An African society once supported a chamber ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like a reversal signal, but here it only means coming behind.
explanation.definitionFit: ECOWAS is the Economic Community of West African States, a regional bloc of nations.

clue.text: Worm getting rid of a goat

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, here a single word of the clue

parts.note: leach is an old spelling of leech, the bloodsucking worm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worm has disposed of a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of LEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A goat is slang for a lecherous man, and a lech is exactly that.

clue.text: Broadcast by a jolly lot, flying fighters

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
taken as written
a jolly is a Royal Marine, and the RM are the whole corps

explanation.surface: A cheerful crowd's radio programme about pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old navy slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An air arm is the aviation branch of an armed service, its airborne combatants.

clue.text: Fibre shown by female, English monarch dismissing Spain

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so the letter for the country is removed

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
E is the abbreviation for English
a queen is a monarch
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Cloth worn by a woman and an English queen who has expelled Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: One E is removed from QUEEN to leave QUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Henequen is the tough leaf fibre of a Mexican agave, used for rope and twine.

clue.text: Show with Eastern wickedness — any number enthralled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern

indicators.note: to be enthralled is to be held captive, so the number sits inside the vice

parts.note: vice is wickedness
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: A display of Oriental depravity that captivates everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside VICE, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or make evident a feeling or quality.

clue.text: Standard set by good Scottish cricket side

parts.note: guid is the Scots form of good
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A benchmark set by a fine Scottish cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like a level of quality but here is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A guidon is a small pennant or flag carried by a cavalry unit, i.e. a military standard.

clue.text: The ____? His art and poet's will be different

definitions.text: The ____? His art and poet's will be different

indicators.note: these letters will be different once they are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
the clue already prints these letters before the blank

explanation.surface: A writer of prose: his craft and the poet's will not be the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram makes THE PROSAIST; the clue prints 'The', so the blank is what is left. The whole clue is also a fair description.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosaist writes prose, and prose is the art set against verse.
